transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. It's really nice to meet you, too. Thank you so much for fitting me in, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

Well, I guess what brings me in is... well, my family was a little concerned about some volunteer work I was doing. I've been helping out at the local historical society, which is usually a really wonderful thing, right? I just wanted to be helpful. But I think I might have gotten a little... carried away? 

I sort of took on their upcoming fundraiser project and acted like I could just run the entire thing all by myself. I mean, I had all these wonderful ideas, so I just dove right in. I started drawing up all these new quilt designs, and I was calling all the volunteers, making up these big, detailed schedules for everyone... and I guess, in my excitement, I ended up promising them some deadlines that I couldn't possibly meet. 

I really didn't mean to cause any stress for anyone, I just wanted to do a good job for them. I hope that makes sense? I just feel a little embarrassed about it now.
During this time, were you sleeping much less than usual and still feeling full of energy?

Well, um, yes, I suppose I was. For a little while, anyway. I was only sleeping maybe a few hours a night, but I'd wake up feeling so refreshed and ready to go. I'd just get right out of bed and start working on my quilt patterns or, you know, making phone calls as soon as it was a polite hour. I just had so much I wanted to do for the society, you know? It didn't feel like a bad thing at the time. I hope it doesn't sound like I was being reckless. 

But lately... well, it's changed. Now I either just lie awake at night worrying about everything I messed up, or I end up sleeping really late and I still feel just completely worn out. It's not very productive of me, I know. I really should be doing better. Does that happen sometimes, where it just switches like that?
During that high-energy period, did you ever hear or see things that other people couldn't?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that. I mean, I know I was a little overenthusiastic with the scheduling and the quilts, but I wasn't... I wasn't seeing things or hearing voices, I promise. 

I just had a lot of ideas, maybe too many, but they were all just my own thoughts. I hope you don't think I'm completely losing my mind? I really was just trying to be helpful to the society. I wouldn't want anyone to think I was acting... well, you know, crazy. That's not what you're thinking, is it?
During that high-energy period, were you admitted to a psychiatric hospital?

Oh, no, no. I wasn't in the hospital. I really didn't need anything like that. I was just at home, doing my volunteer work and, well, maybe getting a little too wrapped up in it. But I was perfectly safe, and I wasn't a danger to anyone or anything like that. 

I just needed to, you know, slow down a bit. My family just wanted me to come talk to you to make sure everything was okay, which I think is very sensible of them. You don't think I should have been in the hospital for just taking on too many projects, do you? I really am trying my best to manage things better now.
After that high-energy period ended, did you go through a time when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I was depressed all day, every day. I mean, I've definitely been feeling a bit down lately, like I mentioned before, just sort of tired and maybe a little guilty about how I acted when I was so busy. 

But I try to keep my chin up, you know? I still make sure my husband has dinner, and I try to keep the house tidy, even if it takes me a lot longer than it used to. I wouldn't want to be a burden on anyone. It's just a bit of a slump, I think. That's normal after being so busy, right? I'm sure I'll bounce back soon if I just try a little harder. I don't want you to worry that I'm completely falling apart or anything like that.
About how many days did that high-energy period last?

Oh, um... days? I'm not sure of the exact number of days, but... I suppose that whole overdriven stretch with the historical society project went on for about five months. Just before everything sort of... fell apart and I ran out of steam. 

I really didn't realize it had been going on quite that long at the time. I was just so focused on doing a good job for everyone and making sure it was all perfect. Five months isn't too terribly long to be dedicated to a big volunteer project, is it? I hope you don't think I was completely out of control that whole time. I really was just trying my very best to be helpful.
During that five-month high-energy period, did your behavior cause serious problems in your daily life or relationships?

Oh, well... I wouldn't say "serious problems," exactly. I mean, my husband has been just wonderful, really stepping up. I did get a little overwhelmed toward the end of it all, and... well, I stopped keeping up with some of my commitments. 

He's had to take over a lot of the household routines for me, which I feel terrible about. And he even had to deal with the historical society folks because I just... I couldn't quite face the people who were waiting on me to finish things. It got to be a bit much. But he handled it so beautifully. It's just a temporary little hiccup in our routine, you know? Couples help each other out like that all the time, don't they? I'm sure it's nothing to be too alarmed about.
During that high-energy period, did it impair your ability to function so much that you couldn’t manage your usual responsibilities?

Well, um... I guess it depends on what you mean by "couldn't manage." I mean, like I said, I did sort of drop the ball on a few things toward the end there. 

I just... I got so behind on the historical society work, and I felt so dreadful about it that I just couldn't bring myself to face the people who were waiting on me. So, my husband, bless his heart, he had to step in and smooth things over with them for me. And he's been doing most of the cooking and the laundry lately, too, because I just haven't been keeping up with my usual routines around the house. 

But I wouldn't want you to think I'm completely helpless or that I've just given up. It's just that he's so good at taking care of things when I get a little... overwhelmed. That doesn't mean I'm completely incapable of functioning, does it? I'm sure I'll get back to my normal self and take all those chores back over very soon.
At any other time in your life, have you had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Well... I suppose "depressed" is a rather strong word, isn't it? But... yes, I have been feeling quite low for a while now. 

Ever since everything sort of blew up with the historical society—when the orders fell behind and all those little conflicts started happening—I've just been stuck in this... well, this very guilty, heavy sort of place. And I suppose that's been going on for... oh, about nine months now. 

But it's perfectly understandable to feel a bit down when you've let people down, right? I mean, anyone would feel terrible after making such a mess of things. I just haven't quite been able to shake it off yet. It doesn't mean I'm terribly ill or anything, does it? I'm sure it's just a normal reaction to a stressful situation...
